questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, stay calm and focus on your driving. Do not take other drivers' actions personally. Allow plenty of time for your trip, drive at posted speed limits, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When being passed, keep your speed the same. Do not speed up. Let the passing vehicle merge back into your lane safely.

questions.question: Why is night driving more difficult?

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because low visibility makes it difficult to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are moving. You can only see as far as your headlights shine.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, you should look:

options.text: Left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look both ways for oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Look left again because vehicles from your left will be closer to you. Check that the path through the intersection is clear before you go.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A road is entering from the left.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a yield sign is coming. Start to slow down when you see this warning.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a stopped school bus with its lights flashing and signal arm extended?

options.text: Go slowly at 15 mph if no children are outside.
Drive at normal speed but watch for children.

questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when you see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm. Stay stopped until the arm is pulled back and the bus starts moving. This rule applies whether you are going the same direction as the bus or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: Bicyclists use hand and arm signals because they do not have turn signals. When a bicyclist extends their left arm straight out, they are signaling a left turn.

questions.question: What does this orange sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange signs mean there is construction or roadwork ahead. Drive carefully in these areas.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Dark areas in your vision when you get tired.
Areas you cannot see using your vehicle's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas you cannot see using your vehicle's mirrors.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check for obstacles near the rear corners of your vehicle. These areas are called blind spots because your mirrors cannot show them.

questions.question: If a pedestrian is crossing in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk, must you stop?

options.text: No, you do not have to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop for pedestrians at all times, even if they are crossing illegally in the middle of the street.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Anything that causes you to swerve.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off the road. It is a major cause of traffic accidents. Any distraction can cause you to miss important signs and hazards that could prevent a crash.

questions.question: If you see animals near the road, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.

questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful when you see animals near the road. They may suddenly jump or change direction. Animals often travel in groups, so more may be nearby.

questions.question: Which action is NOT safe on the interstate?

options.text: Keep slower traffic on the right side.
Go to the next exit if you miss yours.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Keep slower traffic on the right. If you miss your exit, drive to the next one. Do not back up or make a U-turn on the interstate.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:
questions.explanation: Being tired is a cause of bad driving. Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and hurts your judgment.

questions.question: A driving distraction is:

options.text: Anything that causes you to swerve.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A driving distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anytime and anywhere. They can cause accidents, property damage, injury, and death.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes poor judgment and slower reaction times. You could fall asleep at the wheel and crash, hurting or killing yourself or others.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right ahead.
Upcoming sharp left and right turns.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road curves ahead. Slow down to a safe speed.

questions.question: Before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign, you should:

options.text: Press down hard on the accelerator.
Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: Before stopping, check your mirrors to see the traffic around you. Then release the gas and press the brake pedal smoothly to stop.

questions.question: If you drive more slowly than the flow of traffic, you will most likely:

options.text: Interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.
questions.explanation: If you drive too slowly and block traffic, you may get a ticket. Drive at the same speed as traffic, unless traffic is going over the speed limit.

questions.question: As the percentage of alcohol (BAC) in your blood increases, you become:
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures how much alcohol is in your blood. The higher the BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection means:

options.text: You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can go through the intersection. Yield to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When should drivers adjust their mirrors, seats, and steering wheels?

options.text: While backing out of their driveways.
Before reaching speeds of 55 mph or above.

questions.explanation: Before starting your vehicle, adjust the steering wheel, mirrors, and seat. Also check that your brakes and turn signals work.

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.explanation: You must see clearly through all windows before driving. Remove snow, ice, and frost from all windows and mirrors.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.
Keep a safe distance behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep a safe distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Do not drive too close to the car in front of you.

questions.question: Traffic control devices in construction and work zones are:
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones. Be careful when you see orange signs, cones, or barriers on the road.

questions.question: It is unlawful to:

options.text: Pass another vehicle in a no passing zone.
Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: Do not pass in no passing zones, on hills, in curves, at street crossings, or at railroad crossings. Do not pass if you cannot see far enough ahead to do so safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can travel in either direction in this lane.
You are approaching a divided highway.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic flows in both directions on the road ahead.

questions.question: If you are feeling fatigued while driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: If you struggle to keep your eyes open, drift from your lane, or need the radio loud to stay awake, you are too tired to drive. Find a safe place to stop and rest.

questions.question: What is an important step in turning?

options.text: Always move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: Before turning, look behind and to both sides of your vehicle to make sure it is safe. Slow down to a safe speed for the turn.

questions.question: When approaching a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is well away from your path.
Honk your horn as you pass them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is well away from your path.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind person with a white cane or guide dog crossing the street, stop your vehicle. Wait until they are safely away from your path before you drive.
